references.text: The same chapter describes the first shaving on the first day, which this verse completes on the seventh day as part of the cleansing process for leprosy.
The Nazirite was also to shave his head as part of the cleansing ritual, showing a parallel between various purification rites in the Mosaic Law.
The Levites were to shave their entire body and wash their clothes as part of the cleansing, reflecting the same ritual practice.
Washing clothes as part of the cleansing process is a recurring theme in the laws of purification.
Washing clothes and bathing in water at the end of a period of cleansing, followed by being declared clean, follows the same pattern.
Washing clothes and bathing the body in water as a cleansing ritual to become clean again.
The Epistle to the Hebrews refers to washing the body with pure water as part of the cleansing, pointing back to Old Testament purification rituals.
